bullets.title: Nasdaq +2%, SOX +5.5%: AI chip stocks stage powerful single-day rebound
bullets.body: The Nasdaq 100 surged ~2% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped 5.5% as AI chip names led the tape. Micron rose 12-13%, AMD +8%, Intel +8%, SNDK +12%, and MRVL +7% on the session. S&P 500 approached within 1.5% of all-time highs. UBS raised its 2026 S&P 500 year-end target to 8,100, implying ~8.8% upside from current levels.

bullets.title: TSMC planning 5-10% foundry price hike for 2027; main catalyst for semi rally
bullets.body: Taiwan Semiconductor is reportedly planning to raise chipmaking prices by 5-10% starting in 2027, varying by customer and product, to offset rising material, equipment, and overseas fab construction costs. This was cited as the primary catalyst for the Philadelphia Semi Index's 5.5% surge and specifically drove SNDK +12%. Notably, TSMC's own Taiwan-listed shares fell 7.3% after its 77.4% quarterly net income beat, as markets focused on AI model efficiency risk (Kimi K3).

bullets.title: Oil hits five-week high near $91-92/bbl on Middle East escalation; inflation risk rises
bullets.body: Brent crude surged ~2% to a five-week high above $91/bbl (with reports touching $92) as US-Iran military operations continued (9 consecutive days of CENTCOM strikes), Houthis declared a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia causing Saudi crude tankers to reverse course in the Red Sea, and Kuwait reported Iranian drone/missile attacks. Goldman Sachs warned Brent could top $120 if the Gulf chokepoint crisis deepens. US 10-year and 30-year yields extended to two-month highs. Gas prices crossed $4/gallon for the first time in a month.

bullets.title: Fed rate hike odds surge to ~63-64% on Polymarket; futures price 1.5 hikes by year-end
bullets.body: Prediction markets (Polymarket/Kalshi) are pricing a 63-64% probability of a Fed rate hike in 2026, up sharply from 10% in March. Futures markets are pricing approximately 1.5 rate hikes by year-end. Sticky inflation from oil and tariffs is cited as the driver. Treasury Secretary Bessent countered, characterizing the underlying US economy as 'very strong' with core prices stable and 3% GDP growth 'not unreasonable.'

bullets.title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform launches: 10x perf/watt, 1,000 racks/day production claim
bullets.body: NVIDIA officially detailed its Vera Rubin NVL72 platform, claiming 10x better performance per watt vs. Blackwell and 10x tokens/megawatt on DeepSeek-R1 (per CoreWeave measured data). The Information reported NVIDIA may be able to manufacture 1,000 Vera Rubin racks per day, implying ~$630B quarterly revenue run-rate—though the report was met with some skepticism. The Vera CPU uses a monolithic architecture (not chiplet) with ARM licensing, targeting agentic AI workloads. Ecosystem partners CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Microsoft, Oracle Cloud, SpaceX, and Tesla are deploying the system. NVIDIA's Blackwell Ultra separately set a world record pre-training DeepSeek-V3 at 1,648 TFLOPs/GPU.

bullets.title: AMD wins Azure Helios deal vs. Nvidia; Anthropic deal expected larger than Meta/OpenAI
bullets.body: AMD secured the Microsoft Azure Helios contract, marking the first major competitive challenge to Nvidia's AI accelerator rack monopoly. AMD's Helios rack is reportedly priced 40% above Nvidia's second-gen Rubin, betting customers will absorb the premium. Separately, analyst notes raised AMD's TP to $640 (45x 2027E EPS), with 2027E EPS revised up 11%. GFHK expects AMD's deal with Anthropic—anticipated as the third GW-level customer after Meta/OpenAI—to exceed those prior partnerships in scale.

bullets.title: US grid headroom exhausted by 2027/28; energy could hit 20-30% of hyperscaler compute costs
bullets.body: SemiAnalysis modeling shows existing US grid capacity will be fully consumed by 2027/28 and planned utility-scale generation through 2030 is insufficient to meet load growth, driving datacenters toward reciprocating engines as continuous prime power. One analyst noted energy costs are expected to rise from ~10% to 20-30% of hyperscaler compute costs by 2029. Separately, US data centers are projected to account for ~20% of US electricity consumption by 2035, up from 5.9% today.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler AI capex crushing forward FCF; payoff uncertain as AI capex shifts to issuance-based funding
bullets.body: Multiple sources flagged that hyperscaler record AI capital spending has caused forward free cash flow estimates to collapse. One analyst noted the shift: AI capex is moving from FCF-funded to issuance-based (debt), making Q2 earnings guidance directly relevant to bond markets—not just equity investors. AI accelerators currently represent only 15-20% of active NA data center gross watts, with significant headroom remaining in existing facilities before greenfield is needed.

bullets.title: Momentum unwind deepens: Top H1 Russell 1,000 stocks down 25% avg in July
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs flagged a global momentum unwind. The 25 best-performing Russell 1,000 stocks in H1 2026 declined an average of 25.4% in July, with all 25 down at least 8% MTD. Technology sector entered today 4% below its 50-DMA—the farthest below of any sector—while Financials were 5.3% above their 50-DMA. Separately, concentrated leverage in AI names at record-low cross-asset correlation may be masking hidden tail risk.

bullets.title: Polymarket odds on Hormuz normalization at only 31%; severe threat level maintained
bullets.body: Kalshi prediction markets show only a 31% chance shipping normalizes in the Strait of Hormuz before December 2026, implying disruptions extend into 2027. UK Maritime Trade Operations maintains a 'Severe' threat level for the Strait. Hormuz commercial traffic fell to a three-week low following tanker attacks in Omani waters. Strategic Petroleum Reserve sits at a 43-year low of 316.5M barrels (peak was 726.6M in 2009).

bullets.title: Philly Fed services surges to +7.4 from -25.8; labor market slowing (ADP 4th straight miss)
bullets.body: The Philadelphia Fed Non-Manufacturing Activity index jumped to +7.4 in July from -25.8 prior, with new orders rising to +12.5 and employment to +12.4. However, private sector hiring (ADP) slowed for a fourth consecutive week, adding only 16,500 jobs vs. 19,750 prior. Tariff policy is estimated to have cost $1.4M per manufacturing job saved, with $289B in gross tariff revenue collected since January 2025.

bullets.title: Yen at 1986 lows (162.89/$); USD/JPY cross 163 for first time since 1986
bullets.body: The Japanese yen weakened to 162.89 per dollar, touching 163.04 intraday—the first time at that level since December 1986. The move adds macro cross-asset pressure, particularly for Japan-exposed names, and signals persistent yen carry dynamics.

bullets.title: Memory shortage to deepen; SK Hynix CEO warns shortage gets worse before better
bullets.body: SK Hynix's CEO warned that the memory chip shortage will worsen before improving, as AI datacenter demand continues absorbing a growing share of global DRAM supply. Memory prices have already surged this cycle. NAND shortages are separately expected to persist until late 2027 as suppliers upgrade production lines. MU's bullish options flow was flagged as the strongest of the day, consistent with the TSMC pricing story.

bullets.title: Trump signals imminent escalation against Iran; 9 consecutive days of CENTCOM strikes
bullets.body: President Trump made multiple statements that the US would hit Iran 'very soon' and 'very heavily,' targeting any facility producing nuclear weapons. US CENTCOM has conducted nine consecutive days of operations. Iran's IRGC claimed to have launched cruise missiles at Amazon data infrastructure in Bahrain. Kuwait called in Iran's ambassador over alleged attacks on a Kuwaiti tanker in the Strait of Hormuz. These developments underscore elevated geopolitical tail risk.

bullets.title: USTR signals another round of tariffs coming; Canada Section 338 tariffs up to 50% in 30 days
bullets.body: USTR Greer signaled another round of Trump tariffs is forthcoming. Trump announced Section 338 tariffs with a maximum 50% rate on selected Canadian imports effective in 30 days—Canada's Carney called it a USMCA violation and preferred a comprehensive trade deal. USTR also labeled China's AI model distillation as IP theft, setting up potential further tech-sector trade friction.

bullets.title: US 30-year yields at two-month highs; Fed reverse repo collapses to $275M (1 counterparty)
bullets.body: US 30-year yields hit their highest level since May as oil-driven inflation concerns stoked rate hike pricing. Simultaneously, Fed reverse repo usage collapsed to just $275M with only one counterparty accessing the facility, signaling excess system liquidity even as the rate outlook tightens. The juxtaposition of abundant liquidity and rising rate hike odds creates a complex cross-asset backdrop.

bullets.title: SPX approaching gamma resistance at 7,520-7,530; options structure key near-term level
bullets.body: Options positioning analysis (SpotGamma) flags the S&P 500's positive gamma zone resistance concentrated at 7,520-7,530, with a 'soft underbelly' below suggesting weak support if the level fails. The S&P 500 is currently less than 1.5% from all-time highs.

bullets.title: AI capex issuance shift: Q2 earnings now a bond market event, not just equity
bullets.body: As hyperscaler AI capital expenditures shift from FCF-funded to debt/issuance-based, Q2 guidance from major cloud/AI companies will directly affect investment-grade bond markets—amplifying the macro significance of this earnings cycle. Upcoming reports from Alphabet, Tesla, and Intel are viewed as key tests of AI spending conviction and market leadership.

bullets.title: Rare earth waiver expiration in November could cost $6.5T GDP; Xi visit precedes key Q4 risk
bullets.body: Rare earth export waivers from China expire in November, with one estimate citing a $6.5 trillion GDP impact from expiration. A Xi visit to Washington precedes this deadline, framing it as a potential Q4 geopolitical inflection point for tech supply chains.

bullets.title: Bessent: 'At the 1-yard line' on Clarity Act in Senate; crypto regulatory milestone near
bullets.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent signaled the Senate is very close to passing the Clarity Act, a key crypto regulatory framework. Bessent also confirmed the Treasury froze a $130M crypto wallet tied to Iran's IRGC. Robinhood surged 8%+ on the day with Needham raising its price target to $123, citing strength across equities, options, prediction markets, and crypto as HOOD positions as a financial super-app.
